question: Based on internal Commission documents, the Commission is considering allowing countries in the process of EU accession, such as Montenegro and Albania, to designate European Commissioners after they have signed an accession treaty but before all 27 Member States have completed national ratification. Such Commissioners could participate in meetings of the College and contribute to shaping EU legislation1.
The College of Commissioners currently consists of one Commissioner from each Member State, while accession countries may participate as observers without voting rights23. Against this background: 1.
What is the Commission’s justification for the inclusion of Commissioners from Albania and Montenegro in the College of Commissioners before accession?

What added value would Commissioners from countries that are not members of the EU provide to citizens and taxpayers in Member States, and what would be the estimated budget impact of adding Commissioners from Albania and Montenegro?
What Treaty provision provides the legal basis for a national of a non-Member State to participate as a Commissioner in shaping EU legislation before their country’s accession?
Rapporteur, www.rapporteur.com/news/exclusive-candidates-could-get-a-commissioner-before-joining-
eu/. 2 3
Treaty on European Union, Article 17(5). Europeiska kommissionen, https://enlargement.ec.europa.eu/enlargement-policy/glossary_sv.
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (25.11.2026) According to the Treaties, the members of the College of Commissioners are chosen among the nationals of the Member States.

In particular, Article 17 (5), first paragraph, Treaty of the European Union states that the Commission shall consist of a number of members, including its President and the High Representative of the Union for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy, corresponding to two thirds of the number of Member States, unless the European Council decides otherwise.

The European Council has so far retained a College of Commissioners composed of one Commissioner per each Member State. The Commission’s communication1 on preparing for a wider Union of 6 October 2026 encourages closer policy preparation and operational cooperation between the EU institutions and candidate and acceding countries.

It also notes that the Commission will examine structured political participation of acceding countries in relevant Commission activities, in full respect of the Treaties, of the Commission’s institutional autonomy and the principle of collegiality.
Nevertheless, the communication notes that pre-accession participation cannot confer membership of the College of Commissioners or decision-making rights to acceding countries.
